request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row can now have an approver, and that user can approve or reject the person's PENDING claims the way a steward can. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V105__person_approver.sql`, adds an `approver` column to the person table. `Person.java` has a matching field.
- **Server:**
  - A new `POST /api/people/approver` endpoint sets the approver and writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=… by=… name=<name> user=<user>` to the audit file.
  - The person's data sent to the front end now includes the approver.
  - In `ClaimService.changeStatus`, the rule that only a steward can approve or reject now also lets the person's approver through. The existing checks still run first, so whoever opened or last edited a claim still can't approve it, even as approver.
- **Front end:** each person row shows the approver (`person-approver`), with an entry box (`person-approver-input`) and a button (`person-approver-save`). If saving fails, the message appears in the row's existing `person-error`.

**Choices the request didn't settle (easy to change):**
- **Who can set an approver:** anyone except a viewer. The test has a clerk (`uma`) set approvers, so I couldn't limit it to stewards. This does mean a clerk could make themselves approver of a person and then approve claims they didn't open or edit.
- **Saving a blank name** removes the approver.
- **An approver who is a viewer** still can't approve or reject, because viewers are refused before any other check.
- **Transfers and merges** don't carry the approver over to the other sheet or person.
